::: {.why}
You can build these from scratch, so the interesting question is not how but whether, and the parameter count against effective sample size you computed last night is most of the answer.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Fit a small feed-forward model under the frozen protocol and report it against the linear baseline with intervals.
- State the parameter count at which the model reliably fails on your data, measured rather than assumed.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit a small network under the same protocol and nested validation as everything else: a few hidden units, heavy regularisation, early stopping on a purged validation fold. Report out-of-sample R-squared with an interval next to ridge and boosting.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Find the capacity cliff: sweep the hidden layer width from 2 to 256 and plot out-of-sample R-squared against parameter count, with the effective sample size marked on the axis. The shape of that curve is the honest answer to whether capacity pays here, and it is specific to your data rather than to the literature.
:::
:::
